task.title: Finding Frail Members In Existing Data
task.shortdesc: States must check data they already hold before asking a member for proof. Every frail member identified this way keeps their coverage without ever receiving a request.

image.alt: The order of checks: build the state condition list, run 12 months of claims, exempt Tier 1 matches with no request, send Tier 2 and 3 cases for more data and caseworker review, and ask the member for proof only at the end.

step.cmd: List The Qualifying Conditions - Start from the five federal groups and decide which diseases and diagnoses belong on your state's list.
Match Them To Code Sets - Map each condition to ICD-10 diagnosis codes, and add pharmacy or equipment codes where they show severity.
Sort Conditions Into Tiers - CMS offers an optional three-tier framework.

dlentry.dd: Conditions that can be confirmed from diagnosis data alone.
Conditions that need supporting signs, such as frequent hospital use, high-risk combinations of medicines, or medical equipment claims.
Not enough data to decide, so a caseworker reviews the case by hand.

info.note: CMS wrote these tiers around the impairment test the court has now struck down, so confirm how your state applies them.

info.p: CMS also names other sources, including health information exchanges, workers' compensation and short-term disability claims.

step.cmd: Handle Substance Use Records With Care - Records covered by 42 CFR Part 2 follow stricter confidentiality rules, and states are still waiting for CMS guidance on how those rules apply here.
Record The Evidence And Set A Review Date - Note which data confirmed each exemption. Frailty status must be checked again at least every 12 months.

result.p: Members whose records clearly show frailty are exempt before any notice goes out, and caseworkers handle only the cases the data can't settle.
